intro: FANN carries out commercial interior fit-out in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, including partitions, ceilings, flooring, joinery, MEP coordination and finishes. Start with the unit's existing condition, intended use and building requirements so the proposal defines the actual work, responsibilities and handover checks.
description: Commercial interior fit-out in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Define existing conditions, joinery, service interfaces, building approvals, site access and handover for a scoped quote.

sections.heading: Start with the unit, not a reference image
sections.text: Identify the building, floor, approximate area and intended use. Say whether the unit is shell and core, fitted, occupied or being handed over by a previous tenant. Share current photographs, available drawings and a BOQ if one exists. Record what needs a site check rather than treating an old drawing as an as-built record.

sections.heading: Separate retained work from new work
sections.text: Mark partitions, ceilings, flooring, doors, counters and equipment as retained, removed, relocated or new. Confirm protection of retained finishes and access to concealed services before closing walls or ceilings. A clear boundary between existing defects and new work helps the proposal identify exclusions and checks still outstanding.

sections.heading: Coordinate services before closing finishes
sections.text: Place lighting, power, data, plumbing and any equipment interfaces against the agreed layout. Identify who checks existing capacity, prepares service drawings and supplies specialist equipment. Record access panels and maintenance needs alongside the joinery and ceiling details; a visual concept alone does not settle these interfaces.

sections.heading: Release joinery against a named revision
sections.text: Agree reception counters, storage, wall panelling and other joinery against dimensions, materials, finishes and internal arrangements. Name the person who approves drawings and samples. FANN's workshop in Umm Al Quwain supports joinery production, but the production release still depends on the actual quantities, approved details and project programme.

sections.heading: Plan access, reviews and handover together
sections.text: Share the landlord's fit-out guidance, approval status, delivery route and any restricted working periods. Identify who prepares and submits required documents, and separate fees from physical works. Agree site checks, snagging responsibilities, service testing and handover information before treating the preferred opening date as confirmed.

faqs.question: What should we send for a commercial fit-out quotation?
faqs.answer: Send the building and unit location, intended use, approximate floor area, current photographs and any drawings or BOQ. Identify retained finishes, equipment and areas being changed, plus your preferred opening date. Say which details need a site check so the quotation can name the work, exclusions and unresolved decisions.

faqs.question: How do shell-and-core and fitted units change the brief?
faqs.answer: Describe the unit's current condition before agreeing the work. A shell-and-core unit and an occupied fitted unit can have different removal, protection and service-interface needs. Mark what stays, what changes and what requires inspection. Existing drawings help the review but do not replace checking the condition of the actual site.

faqs.question: What must be agreed before joinery production starts?
faqs.answer: Agree dimensions, drawing revisions, materials, finishes and internal arrangements before releasing joinery production. Confirm samples, equipment interfaces and who signs off changes. FANN has a workshop in Umm Al Quwain; the approved details, quantities and project programme determine the production plan rather than a universal lead time for every fit-out.

faqs.question: How should work in an occupied commercial unit be planned?
faqs.answer: State which areas must remain in use before the programme is agreed. Discuss separation of work areas, deliveries, noise restrictions and protection of retained finishes. Record any phased access or service interruptions that need coordination. Do not assume a live office, clinic or restaurant can be worked on as an empty unit.

faqs.question: Who handles building approvals and handover checks?
faqs.answer: Agree responsibilities for the actual building, intended use and proposed changes. Identify who prepares and submits required drawings, arranges reviews and pays any fees. Set out service testing, snagging and handover information in the scope. A previous project or target opening date does not establish approval for a new unit.
